references.text: Simeon and Judah were brothers, both sons of Jacob and Leah. This explains the close bond between the tribes.
Simeon and Levi acted together as brothers in Shechem, showing a pattern of cooperation between the tribes.
Jacob's blessing over Simeon and Levi explains why the tribe of Simeon was scattered and eventually absorbed into Judah's territory.
Simeon's inheritance lay within Judah's territory, explaining the natural cooperation between the two tribes.
During the census, the tribe of Simeon was counted as a separate unit, but they were already closely linked to Judah.
The tribe of Simeon and their settlements within Judah's borders confirm the close relationship between the tribes.
The Simeonites fought against the Amalekites at Mount Seir, showing their military activities in cooperation with Judah.
